$comment: Source of truth for The Model Map. Prices are USD per million tokens. Use null for anything not confirmed against a primary source - nulls are excluded from cost math rather than guessed.

notes.pricing: pin = input price per million tokens, pout = output price per million tokens.
notes.rank: Relative capability score used only for ordering and for the 'most capable here' badge. Not a vendor-published number.
notes.tier: Editorial classification for the five-tier ledger: frontier, work(horse), small (fast/cheap), open (a flagship open-weight release), or spec(ialist, unused for now). Independent of 'weights' — a cheap open-weight model is tier 'small', not 'open'; 'open' here means a large, notable open release. Drives every tier color in the UI: the price chart, hovering a model in the full reference, and the coloring in the 'what to use when' table.
notes.plot: true = include this model on the price-range chart on the home page. Keep this to a representative spread so labels do not collide.
notes.flags: oneGpu = runs on a single ordinary GPU. eu = European vendor. zdr = can be used without vendor data retention. m1 = handles roughly a million tokens of context.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.best: The hardest long-running agent work and deepest reasoning. Thinking is always on. Requires 30-day data retention, so companies that forbid retention cannot use it.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.best: Writing and fixing code across many files, plus complex multi-step work. Tops the composite intelligence index at 60.7 and costs half of Fable 5 for most of the capability.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.best: Everyday production duty: close to Opus quality on code and agents at a third the price. Intro pricing of $2/$10 runs through August 31.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.best: Fast, high-volume work: sorting, tagging, extracting, routing, and cheap helper tasks.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.best: Command-line and multi-step coding plus long agent workflows. Shares the top of the coding rankings with Opus 5. Composite index 58.9.

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro
models.best: Video, images, and dense documents, plus science and factual questions. The leader on understanding mixed media rather than on the composite index.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.best: Cheap mixed-media and general production work. The value pick inside the Google stack, and the least expensive credible closed model that handles images and video.

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.best: Near-frontier reasoning on a budget. The cheapest model in the top 10 by intelligence, which makes it the budget door into the top tier.

models.name: Sonar
models.best: Answering questions about current events with sources attached. Live web search and citations are bundled into the token price, with no separate search fees, which makes this the cheapest way to get grounded cited answers rather than answers from memory.

models.name: Sonar Pro
models.best: Deeper search coverage and longer grounded answers than base Sonar. A separate Pro Search mode adds multi-step agentic lookups billed per thousand queries rather than per token, at roughly $14 to $22 per thousand.

models.name: Sonar Reasoning Pro
models.best: Multi-step reasoning over live search results. The pick when a question needs both current information and actual analysis rather than a summary of the top few links.

models.name: Sonar Deep Research
models.costNote: Varies by query: roughly $0.30 to $1.30 each
models.best: Long research jobs that run dozens of searches on their own and hand back a written report. Billing is unusual: on top of the base token rate it charges separately for citations and for its own reasoning, so real cost lands around $0.30 to $1.30 per query and is hard to predict in advance.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.best: Overall coding scores and math, at 97.3% on MATH-500. Released April 2026, and the MIT license means genuinely no strings attached.

models.name: DeepSeek V4-Flash
models.best: The best quality per dollar in open weights: a respectable intelligence score at under thirty cents per million words out.

models.name: GLM-5.2
models.best: Open-weight coding and long-running agent tasks, where it leads the open field by roughly 17 points. Beats GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro at 62.1%. Roughly 6x under proprietary pricing, though the exact rate varies by provider.

models.name: Qwen 3 235B
models.best: Open-weight reasoning and math: 77.2% on graduate-level science questions and 85.7% on competition math, the strongest open model at both. Apache 2.0 keeps it free of commercial restrictions.

models.name: Qwen 3.7 Flash
models.best: Being the cheapest credible model anywhere, roughly 4.7x cheaper on input than DeepSeek V4-Flash. The pick when you are processing enormous amounts of text and volume is the whole problem.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 (27B dense)
models.best: Private, local work. Small enough to run on a single ordinary graphics card, which makes it the practical choice for anything that cannot leave your own machine.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.best: Very long documents and mixed media, quickly. Handles text, images, and video natively, and runs roughly 15x faster than its predecessor on the longest inputs. One of the highest-volume coding models on OpenRouter.

models.name: Kimi K2.6
models.best: Mixed-media agent work and long-form writing quality. A very large model that only activates a small slice of itself per request, keeping it affordable. Priced around 1.7x MiniMax M3, inferred from published comparisons rather than confirmed directly.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.best: Working across many languages, and European data residency when that matters legally. Strong general knowledge and math. One clear warning: avoid it for code, where it ranks roughly 125th out of 130 models.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.best: Broad general use, with the widest tooling and community support of any open model. Two caveats: the license only allows commercial use below 700 million monthly users, and Meta has moved its frontier work to a closed model, so Llama 4 is likely the last of the line.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.best: Long-running agent workflows: multi-step coding agents, document search across big archives, and orchestration pipelines. Scores 48 on the Artificial Analysis index. NVIDIA published the weights, training recipes, reward models, and datasets under a permissive Linux Foundation license, which is unusually complete as open releases go.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Super
models.best: Cheap production work on very long inputs: a million tokens of context at roughly eight cents per million in, with a free tier on OpenRouter. Renting it is the practical route, since self-hosting at full precision wants eight datacenter GPUs.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Nano
models.best: Long documents on your own hardware. The 30B variant runs on a single 24GB card such as an RTX 3090 while still accepting a million tokens of context, and a smaller 4B variant fits in about 5GB.
